shape._comment: Counted error baseline for `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`. Mirrors the migration-prefix-collisions baseline pattern. The CI gate (scripts/ci/typecheck-no-regression.mjs) fails if a PR raises the count above this baseline. PRs that REDUCE the count should run `npm run ci:typecheck:write-baseline` so the new lower number lands and ratchets the bar tighter for the next PR. Goal over time: 0.

shape.$comment: Tables referenced by server SQL that NOTHING in the repo creates — no migration, no drizzle pgTable, no runtime DDL. Pinned to the exact referencing file set, so an entry cannot silently acquire new call sites. Every entry is a feature that either returns 500 (unguarded query) or silently no-ops (query inside try/catch). Each is a defect awaiting a code-derived migration or a retirement, NOT an approved pattern. Shrink this file; never grow it. See ledger C-11/C-14 for the remediation pattern: derive the shape from the queries, add one canonical migration, prove it with a golden journey.

Pre-existing duplicate CREATE TABLE definitions, pinned to the exact set of files that define each table. Each entry is a defect to be reconciled per ADR-0006, not an approved pattern. A NEW table collision, or a NEW file defining an already-colliding table, fails CI. Shrink this file; never grow it. Standing exceptions (documented in ledger C-8/C-10/C-11): entries whose only rival is a dead root-lineage 0010 file — their canonical DDL lives in db/migrations/20260725_* and ADR-0006 retirement of the dead files removes the entries.

Modules under server/ or client/src/ that nothing in the repository references. This list may only shrink: delete the module, or wire it up, then regenerate with npm run ci:unreferenced-modules:write-baseline. Adding an entry by hand is a regression, not a fix.

shape.description: Files allowed to instantiate an LLM client directly outside the governed AI gateway. This is the gateway-bypass burndown list. Do NOT add to it — route new AI calls through server/services/ai-gateway (getGateway) or the shared client. Removing entries (by routing them through the gateway) is encouraged. Enforced by scripts/ci/check-gateway-bypass.mjs.

Accepted set of env vars read by server/ + shared/ but not yet documented in .env.example. New undocumented vars fail CI; document them in .env.example (preferred) or, if intentional, re-run npm run ci:env-var-docs:write-baseline. Ratchet this list down over time.
